items.caption_verbatim: Figure 3: A schematic for a specific implementation of our automaton-like model.
items.note: Six process boxes and one decision diamond: 'Queue: Desired trip offered?' branches IF NO to 'Visitor Rejected' and IF YES down to Load River, Move Visitors: y*, Resolve Conflicts (If βA > βB Bump B) and Evaluate Visitors; IF YES returns to 'Populate Reservoir of Completed Visitors', IF NO drops to 'Perform Calculations' and loops back to the decision. The condition labels are printed red and green inside the frame, not in a key.

note: Twenty measured regions, twenty accounted: twelve figure rows for the paper's eight printed figures (Figures 5 to 8 are each a surface over a contour, so two rows apiece) and eight counted tables for six printed tables (Table 6 is three stacked grids under one caption). Both registers printed in this paper are measured in full - no printed exhibit is missing and no region is excluded. Declared gap: none. The three figures on p9, p11 and p13 are keyed as raster by the layout pass because each is a single image object, but Figures 1 to 3 are drawn line art that the paper embedded as pictures.
rules: Figures 5 to 8 are each printed as two measured regions - a 3-D surface above its own contour map - under one caption, so each figure is recorded twice, the upper row as surface-or-3D with three_d surface-mesh and a colour bar and the lower row as heatmap-or-contour with a swatch key instead [geometry.three_d] [geometry.colorbar].

Figures 1 to 4 are drawn schematics with no axes, tick numbers or legend, so none of the four carries printed_numbers; Figure 4 is a raster banner whose only content is boat positions and two equal arrows, and it is recorded as flowchart-or-schematic on paper 35's raster-schematic precedent rather than as a photograph [geometry.printed_numbers] [geometry.family].
Figure 4's caption is printed above the banner, the only such caption in this paper, so its caption position is above while every other exhibit is below [caption.position].

Table 6 is one printed table laid out as three stacked grids (number of visitors, percentage off schedule, percentage rejected) sharing one caption, so it is recorded as three counted tables whose caption is the one printed line [table.rows] [table.merged_cells].

Every column of Table 6 is a λ setting whose λ value is not printed; the header carries the symbol alone and the row factor is α, which is why the grid has a merged header cell and no complete column labels [table.merged_cells].

Only two exhibits are named in running text at all: Table 1 is called back to from p10, six pages after the grid, so its mention lead_pages is negative, and Tables 4 and 5 are named together in the sentence that follows them on p14 [mention.lead_pages].

Captions that are followed on the same page by ordinary prose are cut at a named stop: 'Each cell represents' for Figure 1, 'Note that both the Moving' for Figure 2, 'In this particular implementation' for Figure 3, 'Thus, we need only consider' for Figure 4, 'While the static model offers' for Table 2, 'Since our model allows' for Table 3, 'We tested these implementations' for Tables 4 and 5, 'We here consider' for Figure 7, 'Implementation A of our model is 1102' for Figure 8 and 'From these tables' for Table 6 [caption.verbatim].

Figure 2 draws the generalised rules and is filed under 7.2 even though the 7.3 heading prints above it, and Table 3 summarises the control implementations and is filed under 7.4 although the number of section 8 is printed lower on the same page [place.section_path].
